issues.legal_issue: Granting bail is unjustified when the cumulative circumstances, including strong incriminating material and the heinous nature of the alleged crime, weigh against release.
material_facts: The respondents were charged with murder in furtherance of common intention.
The deceased made dying declarations naming the respondents among those who assaulted and burned her; the declarations were the principal incriminating evidence against them.
Two security guards gave statements under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure describing the victim’s cries for help and her being badly burned after the incident.
The alleged attack occurred within premises of a mill over which the deceased’s family and the respondents’ side were in dispute.
The High Court granted bail, reasoning in part that the risk of witness tampering was remote because the dying declarations had been made in the presence of doctors, lawyers and police officers.

The Supreme Court considered the cumulative effect of the dying declarations, the security guards’ statements, the location and context of the attack, and the cruelty and heinousness of the alleged crime, and found the High Court’s reason inadequate.
issues.conclusion: The Court allowed the State’s appeal, set aside the order granting bail, and directed the respondents to surrender, whereupon their bail bonds would stand cancelled.
issues.legal_principle: Whether to grant bail depends on the cumulative effect of the relevant circumstances; no single circumstance has universal validity or necessarily justifies granting or refusing bail. The Court applied the principle stated by the Constitution Bench in Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab, (1980) 2 SCC 565, and held that Article 136 permitted intervention on the circumstances of this case.

rule.if: appeal_against_bail_grant and accused_charged_with_murder and dying_declarations_identify_accused and security_witnesses_support_account and crime_context_strengthens_case and alleged_crime_is_heinous

predicates.appeal_against_bail_grant: The matter was an appeal challenging an order that granted bail to accused persons.
predicates.accused_charged_with_murder: The prosecution charged the accused with participating in a murder.
predicates.dying_declarations_identify_accused: The victim made statements before death naming the accused among those who attacked her.
predicates.security_witnesses_support_account: Security guards gave accounts consistent with the victim having been attacked and set on fire.
predicates.crime_context_strengthens_case: The alleged attack occurred at premises connected to a dispute between the victim’s side and the accused’s side.
predicates.alleged_crime_is_heinous: The alleged offence involved a cruel and heinous attack.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a bail grant in a murder case, and the victim’s statements identify the accused while supporting witness accounts and the crime’s context and heinousness strengthen the case, the bail order is set aside.
